root_cause.text: In crypto/authencesn ESN decryption, the code incorrectly reused the in-place scatterlist layout transformation for out-of-place requests, moving the high-order sequence number bits into the destination buffer and hashing/decrypting from dst instead of preserving/copying data from src with the correct rearranged layout.
root_cause.evidence: The fix adds explicit `src` handling, gates the old "Move high-order bits" logic with `if (src == dst)`, uses `memcpy_sglist(dst, src, assoclen)` for out-of-place decryption, changes `skcipher_request_set_crypt(skreq, dst, dst, ...)` to `skcipher_request_set_crypt(skreq, src, dst, ...)`, and rearranges the hashed data differently when `src != dst`, showing the original bug was wrong buffer/layout handling specifically for out-of-place decryption.

intent_record.what: A new local variable declaration was added in crypto_authenc_esn_decrypt_tail(): `struct scatterlist *src = req->src;`, alongside the existing local variables such as `dst = req->dst`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this introduces a direct local alias to the request's source scatterlist so the function can reference the input buffer explicitly instead of repeatedly accessing `req->src` or relying only on `dst`; by itself this hunk does not change behavior, but it prepares or supports correct handling of separate source and destination scatterlists in subsequent code.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix authenc ESN decryption to correctly support separate source and destination scatterlists instead of assuming in-place decryption.
intent_record.what: The code wraps the sequence-number restoration scatterwalk_map_and_copy calls in an `if (src == dst)` block, adds an `else` branch that copies the associated-data portion from `src` to `dst` with `memcpy_sglist(dst, src, assoclen)`, conditionally advances `src` with `scatterwalk_ffwd(areq_ctx->src, src, assoclen)` before decryption when `src != dst`, and changes `skcipher_request_set_crypt(skreq, dst, dst, cryptlen, req->iv)` to `skcipher_request_set_crypt(skreq, src, dst, cryptlen, req->iv)`. intent_record.how: This makes decryption handle separate source and destination scatterlists correctly instead of assuming in-place operation. This prevents incorrect reads/writes and malformed output during authenc ESN decryption with distinct src/dst buffers.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix authenc ESN decrypt handling for zero authsize and separate src/dst buffers so the hash input is built correctly.

intent_record.how: At runtime this avoids modifying `cryptlen` or reading a tag when no authentication tag is present, and it fixes how the extended sequence number bytes and payload are prepared for hashing when decrypting with separate source and destination buffers. commit a5079d084f8be781aae8a635cab4b179cfea4ebd
Author: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>
Date:   Tue Mar 8 00:04:58 2011 +0000

    crypto: authencesn - Add algorithm to handle IPsec extended sequence numbers
    
    ESP with separate encryption/authentication algorithms needs a special
    treatment for the associated data. This patch add a new algorithm that
    handles esp with extended sequence numbers.
    
    Signed-off-by: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>
bic_trace_step.reason:
The added code clearly shows the ESN decryption/verification path and is enough to assess the root cause. In `crypto_authenc_esn_iverify()`, the code always builds the transformed scatterlist from `req->src` and stores it in `areq_ctx->sg` (`src = req->src; ... scatterwalk_crypto_chain(cipher, src, ...); ... areq_ctx->sg = src;`). It also rearranges the associated data by placing `assoc` and `assoc2` into `hsg` and `assoc1` into `tsg`, matching the in-place layout transformation. However, there is no special handling for out-of-place requests where `req->src != req->dst`.

The vulnerable construct is present because the verify/decrypt callbacks operate on this single transformed layout without preserving/copying the source layout for out-of-place decryption. For example, `authenc_esn_verify_ahash_update_done()` and `authenc_esn_verify_ahash_update_done2()` hash using `areq_ctx->sg` and later decrypt with `ablkcipher_request_set_crypt(abreq, req->src, req->dst, cryptlen, req->iv);`. This means the ESN-specific transformed layout is tied to one SG view and there is no logic to create a separate, corrected destination layout or to preserve source data when source and destination differ.

Likewise, `crypto_authenc_esn_decrypt()` simply calls `crypto_authenc_esn_iverify(req, iv, cryptlen)` and then decrypts from `req->src` to `req->dst` with no branch for out-of-place operation. The fix described in the root cause would require explicit handling for out-of-place requests so that the high-order sequence-number bits are not moved into the destination buffer and hashing/decrypting is done with the correct src/dst layouts. No such handling exists in this initial commit.
